name: bpf
synopsis: int bpf(int cmd, union bpf_attr *attr, unsigned int size);
description: The bpf() system call performs operations related to extended Berkeley Packet Filters (eBPF), such as creating and managing eBPF maps and programs. It allows user-space applications to interact with the kernel for tasks like packet filtering, tracing, and accessing shared data structures.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: The command to perform, such as BPF_MAP_CREATE or BPF_PROG_LOAD.

parameters.name: attr
parameters.description: Pointer to a union containing attributes specific to the command.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the attr structure in bytes.

return_value.success: Returns a new file descriptor for BPF_MAP_CREATE and BPF_PROG_LOAD, or zero for other commands.
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set appropriately.

errors.description: The eBPF program is too large or a map reached the max_entries limit.
The program has been rejected as unsafe, possibly due to invalid memory access or constraints.
Needed resources are blocked; try the call again.
The file descriptor is not open.
One of the pointers is outside the accessible address space.
The command or attributes are invalid.
The specified element was not found.
The call was made without sufficient privilege (lacking CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability).
